question: How high must a 70 kg person climb to burn off one 300 kJ biscuit?
answer: About 110 metres, some 35 storeys. Lifting 70 kg one metre takes about 690 joules, so 110 m is roughly 75 kJ of work. Muscles turn only about a quarter of food energy into work; the rest leaves as heat. So 75 kJ of climbing burns 300 kJ of food: one biscuit, one tower block.
move: Compare how easily something is added with how hard it is to remove.
ask: Where am I trying to undo something the hard way, when not adding it would be easy?
source: Whipp & Wasserman, Journal of Applied Physiology, 1969
reference: Whipp & Wasserman, Efficiency of muscular work, Journal of Applied Physiology 26:644–648, 1969
